form.2. SHORT COURSE DESCRIPTION: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes.
form.3. TOPICS / CONTENT AREAS:
Treatment of this list: starting hypotheses — may add/drop/reorder with justification
A. AI-Native Development: AI-assisted coding, coding agents, developer workflows

B. Agentic Software Engineering: MCP, agent skills, tool use, context engineering

C. Specification & Planning: spec-driven development, requirements to executable specifications

D. Software Development Workflows: loop engineering, iterative development, software factories

E. Engineering Practice: automated testing, evaluation, deployment, reliability

F. Practical Development: hands-on coding, projects, emerging developer tools
form.4. COURSE INTENT:
Central question the course answers: How can software developers effectively
design and operate development workflows in which humans and AI agents
collaboratively build reliable software?

Pedagogical emphasis: Practical, workflow-oriented understanding through
hands-on development and experimentation.

This course should NOT become:
- A general introduction to AI or machine learning
- A traditional programming course
- A purely theoretical treatment of large language models
form.5. TARGET STUDENTS:
Programmes: B.Tech. CSE
Year: 3rd/4th year
Assumed background: Strong programming and software development fundamentals;
familiarity with advanced programming and basic software engineering concepts.
form.11. LAB / PRACTICAL COMPONENT:

Available infrastructure: Student development machines, access to
AI coding tools/APIs, software development environments, and TA support.
form.12. ASSESSMENT PREFERENCES:
Preferred components: Practical assignments, hands-on coding exercises,
project-based evaluation, and a final project.

Components to avoid: none

Rationale: Assessment should emphasize the ability to apply modern
AI-assisted development practices rather than primarily testing theory.

existence.reason: Although CSE701 covers aspects of AI in software engineering and mining software repositories, the new course specifically targets modern AI-native development workflows, agentic software engineering, and collaborative coding agents rather than general AI applications in software engineering research.
existence.recommendation: Proceed as a distinct elective course focusing on practical agentic software engineering workflows.

overlaps.differentiation: CSE701 focuses broadly on research and data-driven methods for software engineering, whereas the new course focuses operationally on hands-on AI-native development, coding agents, and agentic workflows.
CSE594A covers general agentic reasoning for algorithmic and mathematical problems, while the new course specializes in software development workflows and coding agents.
CSE582 focuses on traditional product lines, evolution, and re-engineering, whereas the new course addresses AI-driven development and software factories.
CSE581 covers classical requirements engineering and system analysis theories, whereas the new course targets spec-driven development using AI.
AI501 provides foundational machine learning theory and evaluation, whereas the new course applies tools in an engineering context without teaching ML fundamentals.
CSE201 teaches core object-oriented programming and basic unit testing in Java, whereas the new course builds on top of these skills to use AI-assisted tools and automated workflows.

prerequisites.justification: Students need solid software engineering fundamentals, object-oriented design, and testing experience to effectively evaluate and manage AI-generated code.

supports_topics.reason: Examines automated testing workflows using AI coding assistants.

resource_policy.reason: Because AI-assisted software development is a fast-moving field, a mix of foundational reference books, recent agentic design pattern books, framework documentation, and research papers is used alongside standard software engineering principles.

narrative.course_description: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes. Target students build upon foundational software engineering and programming knowledge to configure coding agents, construct executable specifications from natural language requirements, analyse failure causes in AI-generated code, evaluate automated testing and deployment pipelines, and execute end-to-end AI-native software development workflows. The course is taught through a combination of lectures, tutorials, and practical laboratory sessions involving hands-on coding and project-based work.
narrative.sequencing_rationale: The modules progress from foundational AI-assisted coding and agent skills to specification-driven development, loop engineering, automated testing, and final project integration. This sequence relies on core software engineering prerequisites from CSE201 to ensure students possess the necessary software fundamentals before managing AI-generated code.
narrative.assessment_rationale: The assessment mix comprises quizzes, assignments, a mid-semester examination, a project, and an end-semester examination. This structure balances theoretical comprehension with practical competencies, emphasizing project-based evaluation and hands-on coding as aligned with course outcomes.
narrative.positioning_rationale: Unlike CSE701 which focuses broadly on research and data-driven methods, or CSE594A which covers general agentic reasoning for mathematical problems, this course specializes directly in software development workflows, coding agents, and agentic workflows for software engineering.
